findings.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
findings.summary_md: Original disclosure: on August 31 a new identity theft service called Nexus advertised on the Exploit forum access to scans of more than 153 million US and Canadian driver's licenses, plus 10 million ID cards, 3 million travel documents and 579,000 medical cards. Krebs verified records via consenting victims, matched scan timestamps (in GMT) to Hertz rentals and Planet13 dispensary visits, and observed roughly 400,000 records added in 24 hours, with sellers claiming over a year of continuous exfiltration. The FBI's New Orleans field office opened an official investigation into idscan.net the same day; Nexus went dark hours after publication.

findings.title: I rented a car, and within hours, my driver's license was for sale
findings.summary_md: Dan Goodin's first-person account: a high-resolution scan of his license appeared on Nexus within hours of an employee scanning it at a car rental counter, implying near real-time access to the scanning vendor's data. Each record carried six image files including infrared and ultraviolet captures, which could let cloned counterfeit IDs pass hologram tests. Nexus went dark within hours of the KrebsOnSecurity scoop, removing the only way for people to check whether their IDs were included.

findings.title: IDScan sued over alleged data breach affecting 153 million drivers
findings.summary_md: First news of legal fallout: multiple lawsuits filed in Louisiana against IDScan, with law firms including Markovits, Stock & DeMarco and Hall Attorneys investigating class actions, alleging IDScan failed to protect client data such as Hertz's. Reuters independently confirmed the FBI investigation, and BleepingComputer reported records belonging to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and an FBI assistant director appeared in the service. IDScan had made no public statement at that point, though the firm says business customers were notified around September 1.

findings.title: Notification of Data Security Incident
findings.summary_md: The vendor advisory, dated September 4, 2026: IDScan.net learned on or around September 1 that certain data may have been accessed without authorization and determined an unauthorized third party may have accessed or copied customer information stored within accounts on the IDScan.net cloud, including full names and driver's license or other government-issued identification numbers. The notice states full access to the information required payment, offers free credit monitoring and identity protection (hotline 1-833-516-2980), and says the company is cooperating with federal law enforcement. TechCrunch reported the page was published with a noindex directive keeping it out of search engines.
